extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare billing/compliance officers, health policy stakeholders, and commenters on the FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and explains the evaluative criteria, payment formulas, eligibility rules, and methodological assumptions in the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services' FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule, as relevant to hospital payments, program participation, and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: New technology add-on payment calculation limits (§412.88(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.88(a)(2), the new technology add-on payment for each case is limited to the lesser of: (1) 65 percent of the costs of the new technology (or 75 percent of the costs for technologies designated as QIDPs, approved under the LPAD pathway, or for certain gene therapies when used for SCD); or (2) 65 percent of the amount by which the costs of the case exceed the standard MS-DRG payment for the case (or 75 percent of that amount for QIDP/LPAD/gene therapies indicated above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it is difficult to predict actual add-on payments, CMS estimates in the proposed rule are based on the applicant's estimate at submission and on an assumption that every qualifying claim would receive the maximum add-on payment. Percent limits (65% or 75%) and the two-way lesser-of rule govern per-case payment calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness period requirement for new technology add-on payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Technologies must still be within the 2- to 3-year newness period to qualify for new technology add-on payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies a defined ‘‘newness’’ window (2–3 years) when determining eligibility; technologies outside that window are not considered new for add-on payment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative pathway eligibility for new technology add-on payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the alternative pathway, new technologies that are medical products with a QIDP designation, approved through the FDA LPAD pathway, or designated under the Breakthrough Device program will be considered not substantially similar to an existing technology and will not need to demonstrate that the technology represents a substantial clinical improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if exempted from demonstrating substantial clinical improvement under the alternative pathway, such technologies must still meet the newness (2–3 year) and cost criteria to qualify for add-on payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add-on payments not budget neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: Add-on payments for new medical services and technologies under section 1886(d)(5)(K) of the Act are not required to be budget neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explicitly states add-on payments under this statutory provision do not have to be offset elsewhere; impact on overall IPPS budget neutrality differs from other programs that require neutrality adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS estimation approach for new technology add-on payment impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses the applicant's estimate at application time and assumes the increase in new technology add-on payments for FY 2027 as if every claim that would qualify would receive the maximum add-on payment; where data are limited or unavailable, CMS relies on experience and more limited data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates are preliminary and may be updated in the final rule based on revised or additional information CMS receives prior to finalization. Users should note the conservative 'maximum-per-claim' assumption when interpreting estimated payment impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare DSH / Uncompensated Care Payment (UCP) high-level methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 3133 of the Affordable Care Act, hospitals eligible for Medicare DSH will receive 25% of the amount they previously would have received under the statutory formula, and the remainder (an estimate of 75% of prior DSH payments, Factor 1) reduced by Factor 2 and distributed as uncompensated care payments (UCP) via Factor 3 allocations based on each hospital's share of uncompensated care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor 1 = 75% of former statutory DSH payments (subject to adjustment). Factor 2 adjusts for changes in the uninsured percentage. Factor 3 redistributes the available UCP based on each hospital's uncompensated care share relative to the aggregate. The entire mechanism is explicitly redistributive and not budget neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of supplemental payments for IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible IHS/Tribal hospitals and hospitals located in Puerto Rico receive supplemental payments equal to the difference between each hospital's base year amount (FY 2022 UCP adjusted for aggregate change between FY 2022 and FY 2027) and its FY 2027 UCP, if that difference is greater than zero (42 CFR 412.106(h)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the calculated difference is less than or equal to zero, the hospital will not receive a supplemental payment. CMS provides an estimated total supplemental payment figure but notes individual payments depend on finalized data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data inputs and time window for Factor 3 (UCP) calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, CMS proposes to use 3 years of Worksheet S-10 uncompensated care data from cost reports for FYs 2021, 2022, and 2023 to calculate Factor 3 for all DSH-eligible hospitals, including IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The choice of S-10 years affects hospitals' Factor 3 shares. CMS refers readers to the preamble for full methodological detail; changes to the years or method would alter redistributive outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and aggregation rules in UCP impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS excluded hospitals that terminated participation in Medicare as of Feb 3, 2026, Maryland hospitals, new hospitals, and SCHs expected to be paid by hospital-specific rates; Rural Community Hospital Demonstration participants were also excluded. Data from merged/acquired hospitals were combined under the surviving hospital's CCN and the non-surviving CCN excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exclusions and aggregation rules affect the universe used for impact estimates and can materially affect aggregate and subgroup results; stakeholders should note whether their hospital was included in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation guidance for percent-change results in UCP impact tables
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS explains that a percent change greater than the overall average decrease (approx. -3.3%) indicates hospitals in that category would experience a smaller-than-average decrease, whereas a percent change less than -3.3% indicates a larger-than-average decrease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contextual guidance helps stakeholders interpret relative winners and losers across hospital categories (e.g., rural vs urban, bed-size, region, teaching status, ownership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital payment policy qualifying criteria (post-temporary changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning January 1, 2027 (absent further Congressional action), qualifying as a low-volume hospital reverts to pre-FY2011 statutory requirements: a subsection (d) hospital must be more than 25 road miles from another subsection (d) hospital and have less than 200 discharges (total, including Medicare and non-Medicare) during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimates the expiration of temporary changes will decrease aggregate low-volume hospital payments; distance determinations are evaluated by each hospital's Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC), which limits CMS's ability to precisely estimate continued qualification for some hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation method for impact of low-volume payment policy change
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS applies the same quantitative methodology used for changes in payments per case (discussed in I.G. and Appendix A) to estimate the payment impact of reverting low-volume rules, producing an estimated decrease in aggregate low-volume payments (e.g., $258 million for FY 2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates rely on best available data and include caveats where distance or other data are unavailable; CMS reports counts of hospitals expected to lose qualification and notes uncertainty where MAC determinations are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to prohibit unlawful discrimination by GME and NAH education programs
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes that approved medical residency training programs (and similarly, approved nursing and allied health education programs and accreditors) must not discriminate, or promote or encourage discrimination, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or religion, including use of those characteristics or intentional proxies as selection criteria for employment, participation, resource allocation, or similar activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective date of the proposed policy is October 1, 2026. CMS states it believes no approved programs or accreditors would continue to engage in such unlawful discrimination after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed changes for determining net costs of approved NAH education programs
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes revising 42 CFR 413.85(d)(2) to require that tuition and other revenue be subtracted from the allowable direct costs of a hospital's NAH education programs prior to allocation of indirect costs; CMS also proposes clarifications on allowable indirect NAH costs and requires hospitals with approved provider-operated NAH programs to follow specified procedures to ensure correct indirect cost allocation to NAH cost centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposal stems from a court ruling and CMS notes it cannot estimate the financial impact because hospitals' current cost-reporting procedures (absent this rule) are unclear; hospitals should be prepared to change cost allocation practices if finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) payment-adjustment methodology and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The HRRP reduces a hospital's base operating DRG payments to account for excess readmissions for selected conditions/procedures. CMS will integrate Medicare Advantage beneficiaries into cohort calculations and reduce the applicable period from 3 years to 2 years beginning with FY 2027 program year; CMS proposes to add sepsis as an applicable condition beginning with FY 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the FY 2027 impact analysis, hospitals are sorted into quintiles by proportion of dual-eligible stays; excess readmission ratios (ERRs) are assessed relative to peer-group medians; a neutrality modifier is applied for budget neutrality. Hospitals must have 25 or more eligible discharges for at least one measure during the applicable period to be eligible for penalty assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of the Sepsis readmission measure (proposed for FY2029)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes adopting the 'Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Readmission Rate Following Sepsis Hospitalization' measure beginning with the FY 2029 program year (no change to information collection burden anticipated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS recognizes potential hospital costs associated with post-discharge care coordination and transition planning, and requests comment on financial impacts hospitals may incur to minimize sepsis readmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value-Based Purchasing (VBP) Program funding and scoring approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The VBP Program funds incentive payments via a 2% reduction to hospitals' base operating DRG payments (section 1886(o)(7)(B)); the total pool equals the total reduced payments (estimated ~ $1.9 billion for FY 2027). CMS used prior-year TPSs (FY 2026) as proxies for impact analysis and applied proxy adjustment factors derived from FY 2026 TPSs and MedPAR payment amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses historical Total Performance Scores (TPSs) for proxy adjustment factors in impact analysis. Actual TPSs for the FY 2027 program will be available later for hospital review and correction; impact estimates may change in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) Reduction Program criteria and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS estimates the proportion of hospitals in the worst-performing quartile of Total HAC Scores by characteristic based on previously adopted policies. Measure inputs include CMS PSI 90 (using Medicare FFS discharges July 1, 2022 – June 30, 2024, and PSI v15.0) and NHSN SIRs for CLABSI, CAUTI, SSI (colon and abdominal hysterectomy), MRSA bacteremia, and CDI using surveillance data Jan 1, 2023 – Dec 31, 2024. Hospitals in the worst-performing quartile receive payment reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table-based impact estimates exclude Maryland hospitals and hospitals without a Total HAC Score. CMS allows a 30-day review and corrections period in the fall of 2026 to finalize results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and budget neutrality methodology for the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration (RCHD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 410A statutory budget neutrality requires the Secretary to ensure aggregate payments made under the demonstration do not exceed what would have been paid if the demonstration were not implemented. CMS proposes to continue estimating additional payments for participating hospitals and adjust national IPPS rates ('budget neutrality offset') applied across the payment system as a whole rather than across participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because finalized cost reports were not yet available, CMS is not applying a budget neutrality offset in the FY 2027 proposed rule and instead proposes to include FY 2027 and FY 2028 estimated demonstration costs in the FY 2028 offset. CMS has historically made retrospective adjustments to the offset when finalized cost reports become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: General method for impact analyses when data are limited
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses the most recent available claims data to estimate impacts on payments per case; when CMS has limited or no specific data, it attempts to predict impacts based on experience and other more limited data, and notes where estimates are preliminary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS flags estimates that rely on applicant-provided data or limited information and indicates they may be updated in the final rule. Stakeholders should treat such estimates as provisional and subject to revision upon submission of complete cost/volume data or finalized CMS analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and application processing notes for new technology add-on payments
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS received 47 applications for FY 2027 (32 alternative, 15 traditional); 17 applicants withdrew or were found ineligible. CMS proposes to approve 22 alternative pathway applications for FY 2027, and notes cost/volume information missing for one approved alternative-pathway technology, which was excluded from the payment estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will assess traditional-pathway applications for eligibility later and, if approved, discuss their estimated payment impact in the final rule. Absence of required cost/volume data will prevent inclusion in payment estimates.
